text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's neuclear power plant Kozloduy is expected to discuss the development of bilatteral connections with Electricite de France, Kozloduy's executive director Kiril Nikolov said.
A possible 20 million French francs loan from Electricite de France to Kozlodui is expected to be discussed at the meeting.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Varna shipyard said it posted 2.121 billion levs pre-tax profit for last year.
-- Bulgaria has banned cooking oil exports from April 1, Interior ministry said.
Licensed exporters were allowed to export a total of 30,000 tonnes of cooking oil by end-March.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank expects to finalise shortly the sale of 92 percent stake in the private Mollovbank to the Czech Investment Fund Istrocapital. The new bank is likely to resume operation this month, BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said. Mollovbank was placed in receivership last year.
-- The shareholders of Bulgaria's private Internationmal Bank for Investment and Development decided to boost the bank's capital to 10 billion levs.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to liberalise prices, import and export regulations of foods from June 1, in line with Bulgaria's pledges to the International Monetary Fund, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.

-- The World Bank will extend a 17 year $290 million loan at a seven percent interest with a 3-year grace period to Bulgaria this year, bank's resident representative in Bulgaria Alberto Musalem said.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt fell by around 300 billion levs to some 2.4 trillion levs, Bulgarian National Bank preliminary figures showed.
-- Bulgaria needs some 170 billion levs to complete the spring sowing, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.
The country hopes to secure the funds from privatisation proceeds of soda ash producer Sodi Devnya and cement maker Devnya Ziment.
-- The World Bank may acquire a 15 percent stake in the Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy through its investment arm IFC, Topenergy executive director Sasho Donchev said.
-- Bulgaria's Union of Young Socialists sold foods at 1987 prices in front of the presidency as an April Fool's Day gag. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
